newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants Indian debt paid in hard currency.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants Indian debt paid in hard currency.

text.p: Russia and India are holding talks on converting India's debt to Moscow into convertible currency to increase Russia's revenues from payments, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

"Talks of the kind are in progress," the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. "We are adhering to the practice that we must transfer to settlements in hard currency with all other debtors as we repay our debt in hard currency."
India is one of Russia's biggest debtors and, unlike many others, regularly makes payments in accordance with original contracts.
But payments are in rupees, which are later sold by Russia's state-owned Vneshekonombank at a discount.
The Finance Ministry official declined to say when the talks could be over.
"The issue is very complicated and delicate for both parties, that's why it is diffcult to talk about the timing and prospects of the talks," he said.
Russia, better known to the world community as a big debtor, has recently been trying to get other countries owing it money to pay up.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said last month Russia would step up efforts to get Libya and Iraq to pay.
